$comment: Identity is frozen by artifacts/design/rule-catalog-v1.md. These govern the presentation of consent and of sensitive values. Whether data may be collected at all is a legal and engineering question this framework does not answer.

rules.title: Sensitive values are not exposed by default
rules.description: Values whose exposure harms the user — credentials, financial identifiers, health and identity data — are masked by default, with revealing them a deliberate act.
rules.rationale: A screen is shared, projected, and shoulder-read far more often than its author imagines. Default exposure makes every one of those an incident.
rules.remediation: Mask by default and make disclosure explicit and temporary.
rules.$assuranceNote: Source can show a field rendered unmasked where its name indicates sensitivity. Which values are sensitive in a given product is a judgment no scan holds.

rules.title: Consent is not obtained deceptively
rules.description: Consent is not pre-selected, buried, obtained by making refusal harder than acceptance, or bundled so that agreeing to one thing agrees to another.
rules.rationale: Consent obtained by design pressure is not consent. The user's agreement is the only thing the mechanism exists to establish, and a deceptive flow establishes nothing while appearing to.
rules.remediation: Present accept and decline with equal prominence and effort, unbundled, unselected.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a consent flow is deceptive depends on the relative effort and prominence of the two paths as rendered. A human establishes it.
